title: Classify reversible inward rounding of rational orthogonal maps (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. A rational orthogonal U admits an injective norm-nonincreasing map F:Z^d -> Z^d with uniformly bounded error from U exactly when U is a signed permutation. This holds in every positive finite dimension and permits nonlinear F.

```text
nonintegral column U e_j=a/q, q not dividing n
norm-preserving integer output y at input n e_j
  squared error = (2n/q)(nq-a dot y) >= 2n/q
complete h-grid ball + injection + norm nonincrease
  worst-case error >= sqrt(2h(1-h)/q)
```

The new step extends ywz65's [PR2589](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2589) fixed-phase obstruction to arbitrary-dimensional rational mixing, with an explicit error quantum and existence classification. PR2589's finite-permutation and fixed-restored-helper arguments remain credited premises. Its stronger two-dimensional phase bound is not improved or replayed. Credit also PR2527, Mason Hale / PR2313 and Jose Manuel / PR2298 for the retained interface lineage. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Classical lattice and finite-set arguments are not claimed as new mathematics.

Only six files under `research/rational-norm-rounding/` are added. [Proof](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/eaa967e7e8aa12cc53ec246a5fc00c5f8873a50b/research/rational-norm-rounding/PROOF.md). [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19373516).

## Evidence

- Before: PR2589 treats a fixed phase on a complete two-real-coordinate disk. After: the written proof supplies the rational-map classification and a dimension-independent grid-ball error lower bound. No predecessor scientific executable is imported or run.
- `PASS_RATIONAL_NORM_ROUNDING`: 1,254 exact output candidates in 59 complete sphere streams for four matrices and eleven nonintegral columns; 704 near-boundary arithmetic witness selections across 64 dyadic precisions; all 5,040 permutations of a seven-point ball, with eight contractive permutations; eight rejection controls, an attaining positive quantum, 81 signed-permutation inputs and three premise controls.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized CPython 3.12.15 commands each passed locally in 0.03 seconds, below their 120-second limits. These are check durations, not a speedup claim. Their complete generated hash-bound receipts agree byte for byte.
- Both registered checks and metadata passed. Six-file committed-byte/source-history preflight passed. Official export integrity and declared-input checks passed. Normal and optimized replays passed in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; their complete receipts equal the checkout receipts and all six file hashes remain unchanged.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

Another CPython 3.12 path may replace the local interpreter. The standard library suffices. No generated output remains in the checkout.

## Limitations

Rational U, a complete integer/grid ball, the same input/output grid, injectivity and norm nonincrease are explicit hypotheses. Retained input/history, data-dependent entrance helpers, finer output grids, restricted domains and outward slack change them. The Omega(sqrt(h)) bound is necessary; its global attainability is not established. High-precision output spheres are not enumerated. The finite reference covers dimensions two through four; the universal quantifiers rest on the written proof.

No actual selected native phase/caller is bound. Native realization, physical storage/tapes, relaxed rounding contracts, compiler and outer admission remain open. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed, and all five framework assumptions remain. Lean, Docker, selected cold replay, independent human and formal proof-kernel acceptance are unrun or unclaimed. All registered executable obligations passed locally.

Canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8 and selected PR6030 remained unchanged at submission refresh. The card changes to this scoped precision/restoration theorem. Main, merged/open PRs, live Discussions and reservations were searched; sparse notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

## Open next questions

- Find the least outward norm slack admitting a globally bijective bounded-error rounder for the q=2 four-coordinate fixture. Begin with a complete explicit grid contract; an actual bijection and physical tariff remain missing.
- Bind one selected native caller's entrance fiber, legal domain, norm, grid and complete outputs. Until that binding exists, this theorem is not a supplier rejection.

## Related open work

- [PR6614](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6614) optimizes linear exactly unitary Gaussian-dyadic two-wire approximants; this theorem fixes rational U, permits nonlinear maps and adds norm nonincrease.
- [PR6509](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6509) constructs sum-preserving reversible nearest Gaussian rounding; exact sum preservation is a different invariant from norm nonincrease.
- [PR6534](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6534) constructs two-axis Gaussian grid maps with exact inverse and sum; no inward norm contract is assumed here for that construction.
- [PR6536](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6536) gives a three-axis reversible error optimum; the present obstruction concerns the additional inward norm requirement, not its reported optimum.
- [PR6574](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6574) gives a four-axis sum-preserving reversible map; this theorem does not impose its extra norm premise on that map or compare error numbers from different contracts.
- [PR6438](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6438) constructs unbiased reversible ensembles for the same rational q=5 phase; this result instead requires pointwise norm nonincrease on each fixed fiber.
- [PR6561](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6561) classifies rounding radii under finite-group equivariance; this theorem requires injection and norm nonincrease, without equivariance.
- [PR6540](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6540) retains a seed and residue for reversible fine-to-coarse coarsening, changing the same-grid/restored-state premises used here.
- [PR6542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6542) rounds a sparse shear correction with exact inverse; its nonorthogonal ideal correction is outside this rational-orthogonal theorem.

These relationships use published contracts, with no extra computations auditing another result. The completion refresh inspected all twelve other account open PRs created since the advance CLAIM, through PR6620. PR6614 is already listed above; the other contributions study different objects or quantities. No new matching bound or numerical disagreement was found in that inspected coverage.
